answer.rationale: both releases and regional moves have prior dossier support; on a p99 write-path climb at peak settlement, a rollback is the cheapest reversible step that attacks the most likely cause (release 2h ago, b1 confirms rollback has cleared checkout-error spikes here before without losing writes) while b2 is held in reserve as the next window if rollback does not recover latency, since b2 shows failover has restored latency cleanly during prior degradation; circuit breakers (b4), read-replica routing (b5), and headroom (b3) do not directly address write-path p99 at peak with a fresh release in the change window; not adding capacity (scaling), since heavy settlement writes point at a code/regression cause, not a headroom cause. Escalate: rollout is staged-gated (b6) so a small guarded rollback sub-percent first is safer than a full revert under peak load; cap downside by aborting if p99 does not improve within the verification window.
